passages.title: A Cleaner Playground · Original A2 Practice Text
passages.text: At Sunrise School, the student council wanted to make the playground cleaner. On Monday morning, eight students walked around the playground and wrote down what they saw. They found plastic cups near the benches and pieces of paper beside the basketball court. They did not find broken glass. On Tuesday, the council placed two bins near the main gate and one bin near the court. A teacher explained which bin was for paper and which was for plastic. The council also put a short notice on the school board. It asked students to use the new bins and keep food wrappers out of the garden. On Wednesday afternoon, students from two classes collected litter for twenty minutes. They separated paper from plastic before putting it into the bins. The science teacher counted six bags of waste, but the notice did not report the bags' weight. On Friday, the council visited the same places again. There were fewer cups near the benches. The group was pleased, but it did not claim that the whole playground was perfectly clean. Next week, members planned to check the bins and speak to younger students about keeping shared spaces tidy. They also wanted to ask teachers whether students understood the new signs. The council had not decided to buy more bins, because it wanted to observe how the current bins were being used first.

passages.title: A Trip to the Riverside Market · Original A2 Practice Text
passages.text: Mila and her brother Arman live near a small village river. One Saturday, their grandmother invited them to visit the riverside market. The market opens early, so they left home after breakfast. On the way, they saw a narrow wooden bridge. Arman wanted to cross it, but a sign said that the bridge was closed for repairs. They used a longer road instead. When they arrived, several sellers were preparing their stalls. A woman displayed woven baskets, while another seller arranged vegetables on a table. Mila bought three oranges for her grandmother. Arman carried the bag because Mila was holding an umbrella. Dark clouds covered the sky, but it did not rain while they were at the market. Before going home, the children met a friend who was helping his father sell plants. He showed them a small seedling and explained how to water it. The children did not buy the plant. At noon, they took the same longer road home and gave the oranges to their grandmother. Later, Mila wrote a short note about the trip. She described the bridge, the market, and the friend, but she did not say that the market was the largest in the area. Her note helped her remember what she actually saw. When her grandmother read it, she asked whether the children had eaten lunch at the market. Mila explained that they had returned home at noon, but she had not written about eating anything. Her grandmother thanked them for the oranges.
